Method of Attack: High-yielding investment scam known as 'pig butchering' involving fake cryptocurrency trading apps that initially allow small withdrawals to gain trust, then lock accounts on larger withdrawals
Apps submitted with valid certificates and benign behavior during review, then switched to malicious servers after approval
Use of fake profiles on social media to lure victims to download fraudulent apps from official app stores
Impersonation of legitimate cryptocurrency exchange domains for command and control communication
Attack Vector: Fraudulent apps distributed via Google Play Store and Apple App Store
Social engineering via Facebook and Tinder using fake profiles
Malicious app behavior switched post app store approval
Indicators of Compromise: Apps named 'Ace Pro', 'MBM_BitScan' on Apple App Store and 'BitScan' on Google Play Store
Command and control server domain impersonating bitFlyer cryptocurrency exchange
Use of valid Apple developer certificates to bypass App Store security checks
